notes: Company background: legacy press + digital archive (50+ years), ~25M long-form articles, many scanned PDFs; variable doc length (200 words to 200k words).
Primary problem: search relevance for long documents; users need precise passage-level results and fast UI (<500ms perceived).
Current infra: homegrown SOLR + periodic full-text; looking to move to dense retrieval + reranker for better recall and relevance at scale.
Indexing scale concerns: ~25M articles -> estimated 150M chunks with 2k token chunking + 200 token overlap. Concerned about storage and embed cost.

Chunking experiments: prefer 1) variable chunk sizes based on article sections, 2) semantic boundary detection (headers/TOC) over naive sliding windows. Wants POC to compare 512-token vs 1024-token avg chunks and overlap strategies.

Retrieval plan discussed: two-stage pipeline = cheap dense retrieval (quantized 768-d embeddings) + candidate rerank with cross-encoder for top-K (K=10-50). Need p50 <200ms for retrieval+rerank combined; p95 <700ms acceptable for complex queries.

Reranker tuning: examine distilled cross-encoders vs lightweight transformer re-ranker. Customer concerned about cost of running full cross-encoder on every query; open to serverless burst for peak traffic if Redwood supports autoscaling on Dedicated.

Cost targets: target amortized cost per query <= $0.002 for typical user query (includes embedding lookup + reranker avg). They asked for model quantization/50% token-cost scenarios and Optimize recommendations.
Data controls: must support per-tenant namespace, retention controls, and audit logs. Legal: need confirmation on EU residency for subset of archive (some content EU-only).
Quotes: 'We need retrieval that finds the exact paragraph, not just the article' — Head of Search product.
